I made a second set of fixes, but since your report only says "(rule) failed", I'm still working out what the rule matches. I couldn't confirm these with a search either: the shell needed your approval and I didn't wait for it. All the edits went through without errors.

What I changed in `index.html` this time:

- **Logo links:** the brand links in the nav and footer pointed to `href="#"`, a common placeholder link. They now go to `#top`, an anchor I added at the top of the page.
- **Shell variables:** the `$BEFORE` / `$AFTER` I added last round look like fill-in values too. I took `verdict diff` out of both code blocks and name it in prose instead.
  - The "Read the disagreements" step now shows the real line from your README run: "the models gave one answer on 70 of 80 question(s) they all answered; they differ on 10".
  - The Try it list has a new point: "Every run is kept, and `verdict diff` compares any two of them case by case."
- **Models table:** the `systemone` row said "+ your model's name". It now reads "`systemone`, with the endpoint's model after a colon".

If it still fails, two things are left that a strict rule might catch: the made-up input examples from last round (`text:Where is my card?` and `json:{"amount": 40}`) and the `{"id", "inputs", "expected"}` shape for `cases.jsonl`. Sending me the rule's definition, or approving the search command, would get this fixed in one pass instead of another guess.
